A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoT2 research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, equations, and proofs, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original supervised-training and GRPO experiments on MNNS, ProntoQA, and ProsQA, including benchmark results and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds GSM8K results using Qwen3-0.6B and expanded CoT2 sampling evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces an implemented GSM8K curriculum that introduces continuous tokens halfway through training and fully enables them by 80%. This is a limited training adaptation; the core CSFT, MTS, and Dirichlet procedures remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning beyond v2's MNNS and tokenized five-hop ProntoQA/ProsQA tasks. This materially extends evaluation beyond the earlier structured state-search settings; all original tasks remain.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain their comparator membership, including COCONUT, discrete CoT, and discrete no-CoT. The added GSM8K experiment uses the already evaluated discrete CoT comparison method; Qwen3-0.6B is the shared backbone.

E3.justification: The added GSM8K evaluation introduces Qwen3-0.6B, 2,000-step GRPO training, response caps of 80–160 tokens, 16/32 continuous tokens, and average response length reporting. Figure 2a also extends Pass@k evaluation to CoT2, sampling only its final answer token. These are added protocols; the original experiments retain their settings.

E4.justification: Figure 2a extends temperature and sample-count sensitivity analysis to CoT2 itself. Table 6 adds a GSM8K response-budget sweep examining accuracy and generated length. Existing supervision, embedding-capacity, sparsity, and entropy analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 explicitly identifies the new GSM8K results as single-run results, without accompanying uncertainty estimates. The existing five-run and ten-run averaging disclosures remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v3 substantially extends reported outcomes with GSM8K accuracy/length results and CoT2 Pass@k curves. Table 6 reports MTS accuracy of 41.3% versus discrete CoT's 37.0% at the 160-token cap, but 27.1% versus 27.2% at 96 tokens. At 160 tokens, MTS responses are longer: 114.8 versus 97.3 tokens. Tables 1–5 retain their results.

T1.justification: The main assumptions and propositions remain, but Appendix D corrects the cyclic matrix's wraparound entry, restores the missing scaling constant in the MoE softmax limit, and revises partial-sum indexing, normalization prose, and the gated-MLP formula. These are localized mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about continuous supervision, parallel reasoning, expressivity, statistical efficiency, and reinforcement learning. The added experiments support these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Remark 1 adds an argument that base decoding's extra O(vd) operation has minor practical overhead. Appendix C.2 frames GSM8K findings as preliminary and constrained by model size and decoding budgets. Section 5.3 nevertheless describes accuracy and length benefits more uniformly than Table 6 supports.

D1.justification: The new GSM8K block documents the curriculum, continuous-token allocations, learning rate, training steps, batch size, gradient accumulation, and GRPO parameters. Existing preprocessing, hardware, PyTorch implementation, and code-access disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds BREAD by Zhang et al. and connects the method to curriculum-based reinforcement learning. The broader positioning relative to COCONUT, CODI, CCOT, Soft Thinking, and other related work remains.

P1.justification: v3 fixes awkward sentences, clarifies sampling explanations, and gives Appendix D an introductory roadmap and four numbered subsections. The original narrative and section order largely remain; author-affiliation and acknowledgement text also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2a is redrawn with both methods' temperature curves, while its earlier single-shot comparison is preserved as Figure 11. v3 adds Table 6, reformats Tables 1 and 5, and adds abstract shading. Most existing displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Relative to v2, v3 provides a more balanced Pass@k comparison, evidence of applicability beyond structured tasks, and localized proof corrections. These improve evaluation relevance and mathematical precision. The gains remain limited by single-run GSM8K experiments on one small model with short budgets, and Section 5.3 overstates Table 6's mixed accuracy and response-length findings.
